column1: This table synthesizes 22 representative studies (2010–2025) that inform the Technology Leverage Score (TLS) model.
Each paper illustrates how digital technologies substitute for labor, capital, or expertise in entrepreneurial ventures.

column2: Citation
column7: Key Finding

column2: **Brynjolfsson & McAfee (2014) – *The Second Machine Age***
column7: Automation substitutes routine labor and increases productivity.

column2: Nambisan (2017) – *Digital Entrepreneurship*
column7: Digital tools expand entrepreneurial affordances beyond local context.

column2: Autio et al. (2018) – *Digital Affordances and Ecosystems*
column7: Digital ecosystems lower entry barriers and reduce capital requirements.

column2: Bhatt et al. (2019) – *IT and Capital Efficiency in SMEs*
column7: Cloud reduces upfront capital investment and enhances operational efficiency.
column10: Does not capture automation or human substitution.

column2: Davenport & Ronanki (2018) – *AI for the Real World*
column7: AI augments managerial decisions and replaces expert human tasks.
column10: No direct link to SME outcomes.

column2: OECD (2022) – *SME Digitalization Outlook*
column7: Digital maturity positively correlates with productivity and resilience.

column2: Müller et al. (2023) – *Digital Transformation in SMEs*
column7: Digital tools improve flexibility and process performance.

column2: Li et al. (2021) – *Platform Scaling and Firm Growth*
column7: Platform adoption accelerates scaling with limited headcount.

column2: Chen et al. (2015) – *Big Data and Value Creation in SMEs*
column7: Data analytics enables resource reallocation and higher ROI.

column2: Bharadwaj et al. (2013) – *Digital Business Strategy*
column7: Integrating IT strategy into firm core enhances competitiveness.

column2: Giones & Brem (2017) – *Digital Technology and Entrepreneurship*
column7: Startups leverage digital tools to scale faster than resource-based peers.

column2: Prasad & Junni (2017) – *Digital Transformation and Dynamic Capabilities*
column7: Firms that reconfigure digital assets achieve greater agility.

column2: Loebbecke & Picot (2015) – *Reflections on Digitization and Automation*
column7: Digitization replaces cognitive and manual tasks, boosting productivity.

column2: Bresciani et al. (2021) – *Digital Transformation in SMEs: Trends and Future Research*
column7: Tech adoption linked to growth and innovation in resource-constrained firms.

column2: Li & Chan (2020) – *AI-Driven Process Optimization in SMEs*
column7: AI tools automate logistics and reduce operational costs.

column2: Vial (2019) – *Understanding Digital Transformation*
column7: Technology creates value through new processes and business models.

column2: Rachinger et al. (2019) – *Digitalization and Business Models in SMEs*
column7: SMEs adopting tech achieve scalable, low-cost business models.

column2: Kraus et al. (2021) – *Digital Transformation in Entrepreneurship Research*
column7: Digitization enables flexibility, but measurement diversity limits comparability.

column2: Yoo et al. (2012) – *The Digitization of Innovation*
column7: Digitization allows rapid scaling with minimal additional labor.

column2: Parida et al. (2016) – *Digitalization and SME Growth*
column7: Early digital adopters show higher growth rates and export performance.

column2: Nambisan et al. (2019) – *Digital Innovation and Entrepreneurship: Research Directions*
column7: Digital innovation reduces capital and expertise barriers.

column2: OECD (2023) – *AI and Productivity in SMEs*
column7: AI-enabled automation drives measurable labor productivity increases.

column1: These 22 studies collectively support the conceptual and empirical foundation for the Technology Leverage Score (TLS).
They validate the idea that **technology substitutes for labor, capital, and expertise**, enabling operational leverage measurable through TLS.
